Streets, schools and getting around Forest Glen BS

items.t: Forest Glen is the Burnaby South sub-area between Metrotown and Edmonds, framed by Kingsway, Willingdon Avenue, Bond Street and Nelson Avenue, mixing the Kingsway condo corridor with detached residential streets. It is named for Forest Glen Park at 4855 Bond Street.

Where the condo stock concentrates: two pockets. The Hazel Street tower cluster at the Metrotown edge, and the older Nelson Avenue / McMurray Avenue / Sanders Street low-rise and tower stock toward Burnaby South Secondary. The streets between are detached houses.

Schools: Clinton Elementary (5858 Clinton Street), École Inman (3963 Brandon Street), Nelson Elementary (4850 Irmin Street), École Marlborough (6060 Marlborough Avenue) and Burnaby South Secondary (5455 Rumble Street).

Transit: route 110 runs on Bond Street and Nelson Avenue themselves (Metrotown–Lougheed via Willingdon, Deer Lake Parkway, Winston and Government) — the sub-area's own streets carry the bus, not just its edges.
Anchors: Wesburn Community Centre at 4781 Parkwood Avenue; Burnaby Hospital sits immediately north-east of the sub-area.
Planning frame: the Cascade Heights Community Plan was adopted in March 2025.

blocks.text: Good to know about Forest Glen BS

items.t: The "-bs" is a filing tag, not a place. "Forest Glen BS" is the MLS's Burnaby South designation; the park, schools and streets all just say Forest Glen. Searches and document requests that include "BS" as a name will miss records.

One building holds a fifth of the sub-area's identity. Sussex's 321 suites (41 storeys, built 2022) make it larger than several of the 1980s–90s Hazel towers combined; sub-area listing counts skew toward it whenever its owners list in number.
The same complex gives two different pet answers.

The hospital is the sub-area's north-east neighbour. Burnaby Hospital (3935 Kincaid Street, Fraser Health) sits immediately north-east of Forest Glen, and the Edmonds Urgent and Primary Care Centre is at #201-7315 Edmonds Street — the two care anchors for the whole Metrotown-to-Edmonds band.

blocks.text: Local rules that affect townhome buyers in Forest Glen BS

items.t: Form B diligence (Oakwood's strata, and each small strata project): Strata Property Act s. 59 — the Form B states the lot's monthly strata fees, amounts owing, approved special levies still payable, the CRF balance and an insurance summary, with the rules, current budget, any Rental Disclosure Statement and the most recent depreciation report attached; provided within 7 days, maximum $35 plus up to 25 cents per page. In a four-lot strata the Form B package is short — read all of it, including who the other owners are and what the CRF actually holds.

Depreciation reports — the small-strata edge case, stated precisely: since July 1, 2024, strata corporations with five or more lots must obtain a depreciation report every five years, not deferrable by vote. Oakwood is well over the threshold; a four-unit Buxton or Elgin strata is under it — no statutory depreciation report is required, so the buyer must substitute their own building-condition diligence. CRF minimum: since Nov 1, 2023, at least 10% of the annual operating budget must go to the contingency reserve fund — in a four-lot strata that minimum builds a very small reserve in absolute dollars.

Taxes and rebates (any new-build purchase — directly relevant to the 2026 Buxton/Elgin/Dufferin product): PTT (1% on the first $200,000, 2% to $2M, 3% to $3M, 5% above) + exemptions (first-time buyers — exempt on the first $500,000 at fair market value $835,000 or less, partial to $860,000; newly built home exemption — full to $1,100,000, eliminated at $1,150,000); FTHB GST rebate — Bill C-4, Royal Assent March 13, 2026 per CRA News No. 122 (100% to $1M, phasing to $1.5M, max $50,000, agreements Mar 20, 2025–2031); New Housing Rebate 36% / max $6,300 / $350K–$450K phase-out; HBP $60,000; FHSA $40,000 lifetime / $8,000 per year; CMHC premiums 0.6%–4.5%. 5% GST applies to new construction (the 2026 multiplex units), not resales — and the new-home warranty position on a four-lot strata project is a diligence item in its own right.

blocks.text: Good to know about Forest Glen BS

items.t: The bus runs on the house streets themselves. Route 110's published path runs through the area's north side via Willingdon, Bond, Nelson, Bennett and Bonsor to Metrotown Station — the same Bond and Nelson streets that hold Forest Glen Park and the detached stock — and onward to Sperling and Lougheed stations in the other direction: a two-direction transit story for the house streets, not just the towers.
Attached outweighs detached more than three to one in listings.

The four-lot strata is the new diligence trap. A 2026 Buxton or Elgin buyer gets strata tenure without the five-lot depreciation-report duty, a CRF built on a 10%-of-a-small-budget minimum, and three neighbours whose votes decide every major repair — none of which shows in the listing's "townhouse" label.

The zoning bylaw most guides still cite no longer exists. Burnaby Zoning Bylaw 2026 (No. 14815) repealed and replaced the 1965 bylaw effective July 1, 2026, and repackaged the districts into a height-based framework — any Forest Glen page quoting 1965-bylaw district numbers is quoting repealed law.

The park is small; the name is big. The sub-area takes its name from Forest Glen Park at 4855 Bond St, a neighbourhood park on the City's parks list — the larger green spaces buyers picture (Central Park west, Deer Lake Park north) sit at or beyond the sub-area's edges.

blocks.text: Local rules that affect land buyers in Forest Glen

items.t: New small-strata diligence: Read the specific project's disclosure/Form B and warranty enrolment, not marketing copy.

Bare-land strata rules (applies to any bare-land strata lot and to the small strata multiplex lots above): Form B diligence (fees, amounts owed, levies, CRF balance, insurance summary; provided within 7 days, max $35 + 25¢/page); depreciation reports on a 5-year cycle for stratas with 5+ lots since July 1, 2024 (a four-lot project sits under the 5+ threshold on the rule as stated — confirm the specific plan's position); minimum 10% CRF contribution since November 1, 2023; rental-restriction bylaws void since November 24, 2022 (short-term restrictions may still apply by bylaw); only 55+ age bylaws valid under SPA ss.123.1/123.2, with May 1, 2023 exemptions (younger spouse/partner, caregivers, legacy residents, defined children); a listing's "45+" line is not a valid BC age bylaw.

ALR rules (for completeness — no Forest Glen ALR parcel is confirmed here): subdivision within the ALR requires ALC approval; ALR residences cannot be stratified (ALC Bulletin 09 s. 6; SPA s. 239; ALCA s. 21(1)); ALC residence caps: principal ≤500 m², suite within principal only, additional residence 90 m² (≤40 ha) / 186 m² (>40 ha). Farm class is three-tiered ($2,500 on 0.8–4 ha; $2,500 + 5% of value over 4 ha; $10,000 under 0.8 ha; applications by Oct 31) — a flat "$2,500+" line is an error.
